page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.small is an entry-tier virtual server from the shared instance family, designed for low-demand computing requirements. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, it features 1 vCPU allocated on a shared basis from an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512, BMI2, and AES. System memory is sized at 2.0 GB, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance type contains no integrated local storage and includes no dedicated graphics processing units, necessitating external disk attachments for stateful persistence. Furthermore, its baseline network throughput is rated at 0 Gbps.

Performance metrics place the ecs.n4.small instance within lower comparative percentiles due to its single shared vCPU configuration. In synthetic compute benchmarks, it registered a stress-ng score of 1061.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 1277.65, alongside an encryption score of 400.02. Memory bandwidth testing demonstrates cached small-block read speeds of 79.26 GB/sec, falling to 8.61 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 7.28 GB/sec for large-block writes. Application-level evaluations show Redis handling approximately 1.22 million SET operations per second and static web throughput reaching 1.22 GB/sec. When evaluating small language model inference with a 135M parameter model, prompt processing attained 128.79 tokens per second and text generation reached 38.66 tokens per second.

From a cost efficiency perspective, ecs.n4.small offers an accessible, minimal hardware allocation suited for organizations aiming to control infrastructure expenses on non-critical processes. The shared core model introduces potential compute contention during peak host activity, while the absence of bundled local storage and zero baseline network bandwidth require careful architectural consideration. Consequently, the instance is best fitted for dev-test setups, continuous integration workers with modest dependencies, lightweight background cron utilities, small reverse proxies, and low-traffic static web servers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.small is a shared entry-level instance positioned for budget-sensitive and lightweight cloud workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization, it provides 1 shared vCPU powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock of 2.5 GHz, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. The instance does not bundle local storage, requiring reliance on remote block storage, and includes no GPU hardware or baseline network bandwidth guarantee. In benchmark evaluations, such as the stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 1061.69 and PassMark CPU score of 1277.65, the configuration exhibits low throughput typical of single-thread shared hardware, placing it in the lower performance brackets. Memory bandwidth also reflects constrained throughput at 8.61 GB/sec for large block reads. The ecs.n4.small instance provides an economical entry point for low-traffic web serving, development environments, background monitoring agents, and light microservices where consistent compute intensity is not necessary.
